dialog|deedee.direction: smiling, affectionate, bright and youthful, never stern

items.text: Tom! Oh, thank goodness. You already have her. She hasn't slept since Sunday.
items.script: [relieved, fast-talking, frazzled mom] Tom! Oh, thank [emphasized] GOOODNESS. You already have her. [exhausted laugh] She hasn't slept since Sunday.

items.text: Michael! Isla is near the curb. Okay. Never mind. Thank you, babe.
items.script: [calling out, alarmed, then sheepish] [shouting] Michael! Isla is near the curb. [beat] Okay. [relieved] Never mind. Thank you, babe.

items.text: My lasagna is a brick. A cold lasagna brick. Michael is guarding it with his life.
items.where: Chapter 8, Olivia at the block party
items.script: [wry, deadpan, exhausted] My lasagna is a brick. A [emphasized] COOOLD lasagna brick. [dry] Michael is guarding it with his life.

items.text: Zero car keys and one very sticky toddler. Wait. Keys. Gutter. Right.
items.script: [tired, deadpan] Zero car keys and one very sticky toddler. [pause] Wait. [realizing] Keys. [beat] Gutter. [flat] Right.

items.text: Cold lasagna, one diaper bag, and Isla eating the tablecloth. We're thriving.
items.where: Chapter 8, Michael at the block party
items.script: [calm, deadpan, tired dad] Cold lasagna, one diaper bag, and Isla eating the tablecloth. [dry] We're thriving.

items.text: Hey, Tom. Good to see you. Please ignore the cracker crumbs. They live here now.
items.script: [warm, deadpan, tired] Hey, Tom. Good to see you. [dry] Please ignore the cracker crumbs. They live here now.

items.text: I heard Olivia say Michael. Whatever it is, I'm on it. Isla, that is not a snack.
items.script: [calm, tired, then firm] I heard Olivia say Michael. Whatever it is, I'm on it. [firmly, to a toddler] Isla, that is not a snack.

items.text: Yes, Olivia. Heard you. Handled. Lachlan, we do not lick the fence.
items.script: [calm, deadpan] Yes, Olivia. Heard you. Handled. [patient, to a toddler] Lachlan, we do not lick the fence.

items.text: Go. GO. I have a house to decorate and a cake to hide from your father. Take the girls and get the scoops.
items.script: [heavy Long Island accent, bossy, hurried, laughing] Go. [emphasized] GOOO. I have a house to decorate and a cake to hide from your father. Take the girls and get the scoops.

items.text: Not today, honey. The cake is in the oven and the oven doesn't care that it's a birthday.
items.script: [warm, gently teasing] Not today, honey. The cake is in the oven and the oven doesn't care that it's a birthday.

items.text: Ice cream? My knee says sit. My knee has been saying sit since 1994.
items.script: [deep gravelly voice, thick New York accent, grumbling] Ice cream? My knee says sit. [dry] My knee has been saying sit since [emphasized] NINETEEN NINETY-FOUR.

items.text: Present. Window seat, please. I won't be reclining.
items.script: [dry, calm, smug] Present. [beat] Window seat, please. [deadpan] I won't be [emphasized] RECLIIINING.

items.text: But I've been on this ladder for an hour!
items.script: [exasperated, wobbling, pleading] But I've been on this [emphasized] LAAADDER for an hour!

items.text: I've only had six lessons, okay?
items.script: [defensive, bossy, embarrassed nine-year-old] I've only had [emphasized] SIIIX lessons, okay?

items.text: Hold that pose. Perfect, don't move.
items.script: [bossy, bright, directing a photo shoot] Hold that pose. [emphasized] PERFECT, don't move.

items.text: Hold still, you need more sparkle!
items.script: [bossy, bright, gleeful] Hold still, you need more [emphasized] SPAAARKLE!

items.text: No dairy, thank you. Almond milk, please!
items.script: [heavy Long Island accent, prim and polite, then fierce] No dairy, thank you. [sharp] [emphasized] AAALMOND milk, please!

items.text: Great take. I wouldn't change a single stitch.
items.script: [warm, sincere, easygoing] Great take. [soft chuckle] I wouldn't change a single stitch.

items.text: A single pea. Foraged at dawn. Finished with the chef's intention.
items.script: [hushed, fancy waiter, reverent] A single pea. [whispering] Foraged at dawn. [proud] Finished with the chef's [emphasized] INTEEENTION.

items.text: Rule one: we do NOT split up. Rule two: see rule one.
items.script: [calm, horror-movie buff, deadpan] Rule one: we do [emphasized] NOOOT split up. Rule two: [dry] see rule one.

items.text: Tiny change. Just one more thing. And one more. And...
items.script: [innocent, then increasingly frantic project manager] Tiny change. [cheerful] Just one more thing. [faster] And one more. [trailing off] And...

items.text: I was throwing a bowl. Literally. ...Wait, come back, I have more!
items.script: [laughing, cheerful potter] I was throwing a bowl. [emphasized] LITERRRALLY. [beat] [panicked laugh] ...Wait, come back, I have more!

items.text: It's just around the bend. ...This bend. Okay, THAT bend.
items.script: [easygoing hiker, cheerful, then sheepish] It's just around the bend. [beat] ...This bend. [mock-confident] Okay, [emphasized] THAAAT bend.

items.text: Jojo, you're up. ...Jojo. JOJO. ...Nice.
items.script: [easygoing, calling to his sister, then louder] Jojo, you're up. [beat] ...Jojo. [shouting] [emphasized] JOOOJO. [beat] [relieved, impressed] ...Nice.

items.text: Coffee run. I got you the usual.
items.script: [warm, easygoing, casual] Coffee run. [affectionate] I got you the usual.

items.text: Fourteen courses. Four seconds. And the check.
items.script: [crisp, elegant waiter, deadpan] Fourteen courses. Four seconds. [dry, slow] And the [emphasized] CHEEECK.
